title: On the Complexity of Bayesian Signal Processing
abstract: arXiv:2608.29840v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We develop a computational framework for Bayesian decision-making. We show that as long as no action is optimal in every state, Bayes-optimal choice is intractable. This hardness need not arise from large action, state, or signal spaces, nor from a complicated represented utility function: extracting enough information from a hard-to-interpret signal to act optimally can itself be computationally hard. We also characterize tractability across approximation notions and identify their sources of difficulty. Under the probably approximately correct criterion, sample-based Bayesian learning is tractable if and only if the signal support is bounded. Our results provide justifications for bounded rationality, costly Bayesian inference, and sample-based Bayesian learning.

translated_title: 论贝叶斯信号处理的计算复杂性
translated_abstract: 我们为贝叶斯决策制定开发了一个计算框架。我们证明，只要不存在在每种状态下都是最优的行动，贝叶斯最优选择在计算上就是难以求解的。这种困难不必源于庞大的行动、状态或信号空间，也不必源于复杂的效用函数表示：从难以解读的信号中提取足够的信息以采取最优行动，这本身在计算上就可能是困难的。我们还刻画了各种近似概念下的可解性，并识别了其困难的来源。在可能近似正确（PAC）准则下，基于样本的贝叶斯学习是可解的，当且仅当信号的支持是有界的。我们的结果为有限理性、有代价的贝叶斯推断以及基于样本的贝叶斯学习提供了理论依据。
tldr: 本文证明只要不存在在所有状态下都最优的行动，贝叶斯最优决策在计算上就是不可解的，且这种困难可能源于信号解读本身，从而为有限理性、有代价的贝叶斯推断和基于样本的贝叶斯学习提供了理论依据。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that Bayes-optimal choice is computationally intractable whenever no action is optimal in every state—a hardness that can arise from interpreting signals themselves—thereby providing justifications for bounded rationality, costly Bayesian inference, and sample-based Bayesian learning.
